channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Urges Public Not to Praise Government or Him
item.description: The President of Kyrgyzstan has asked citizens not to praise the government or himself. This statement encourages a focus on constructive criticism and accountability rather than public adulation. The president's request aims to foster a more objective evaluation of governance.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers Complete Ban on Energy Drink Production and Import
item.description: The Kyrgyz government will review a potential ban on energy drink production and import within a month, following a presidential directive. President Sadyr Japarov cited health risks associated with increased consumption. The move could impact budget revenues by approximately 1.5 billion soms.

item.title: Afghanistan U19 Cricket Team Defeats Malaysia by Ten Wickets
item.description: Afghanistan's U19 cricket team secured a dominant ten-wicket victory against Malaysia in their second Asia Cup match. Malaysia was bowled out for just 42 runs, setting a low target that Afghanistan chased down without losing any wickets in the third over.

item.title: Taliban Intelligence Confirms Arrest of Former Afghan Police Commander
item.description: Taliban intelligence media has confirmed the arrest of Allahdad Fadaei, a former Afghan police commander. The outlet claims Fadaei worked for the 'United Afghanistan Front' led by Sami Sadat, a claim the front denies, calling the audio messages 'fake and AI-generated'.

item.title: Uzbekistan Energy Ministry Warns of Possible CNG Station Restrictions Due to Cold Snap
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Energy has warned of potential temporary restrictions on compressed natural gas (CNG) stations from November 9-11 due to a cold snap and predicted frosts. Gas supply will prioritize residential areas, schools, kindergartens, and hospitals. This is a recurring issue during colder months, affecting many drivers who rely on CNG.

item.title: Tashkent to Begin Heating Season on November 9th, Officials Announce
item.description: Tashkent will commence its heating season on November 9th, with heat supply to social institutions like schools and hospitals starting on the same day. Residential buildings will also gradually receive heat. The cost of heating will be charged from the actual connection date, as documented by the management company. Residents with uneven heat distribution are advised to contact their management company.

item.title: Kabul University Reopens Amidst Taliban Rule and Women's Protests
item.description: Kabul University reopened on September 6, 2022, months after the Taliban takeover. Women's protests demanding "Bread, Work and Freedom" continued across the city, challenging Taliban rule despite facing repression. Their resistance is highlighted as a significant historical event.

item.title: US Offers Up to $20 Million Reward for Information on Iran's Nuclear Program
item.description: The U.S. Department of State is offering up to $20 million for information regarding Iran's nuclear program through its "Rewards for Justice" program. The announcement seeks details on facilities, equipment, personnel, and technical aspects. This comes amid ongoing diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions between the US and Iran.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Tajikistan Presidents Inaugurate New Embassy Complex in Astana
item.description: Presidents Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Emomali Rahmon inaugurated the new Tajik Embassy complex in Astana. The leaders discussed trade, transport, and energy, signing a joint statement on further cooperation. Tokayev awarded Rahmon the Qoja Ahmet Yasaui order, recognizing his contributions to bilateral relations and regional stability.

item.title: US Midterm Election Results Signal Dissatisfaction with Trump Policies
item.description: Democrats' victory in the US midterm elections, securing majorities in Congress, indicates public dissatisfaction with Donald Trump's policies, particularly on the economy and foreign affairs. This outcome places greater constraints on the president, especially regarding potential military actions and budgets.

item.title: Kazakhstan Reviews Social Assistance Rules to Prioritize Low-Income Families
item.description: Kazakhstan is revising its social assistance rules to better assess family needs, aiming to prioritize low-income households. Political scientist Eduard Poletaev suggests this approach will prevent aid from reaching families who can support themselves, ensuring resources benefit those most in need, as highlighted by President Tokayev.

item.title: Tajikistan President Emomali Rahmon Concludes Official Visit to Kazakhstan
item.description: The official visit of Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon to Kazakhstan has concluded. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev saw off the distinguished guest at the capital's airport. The leaders had previously attended the opening ceremony of the new building of the Tajik Embassy in Astana.

item.title: COP31: Details on the 31st UN Climate Change Conference Scheduled for November 2026
item.description: The 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) is set to take place from November 9-20, 2026, in Antalya, Turkey. The conference, a major global forum for climate action, will be chaired by Murat Kurum, with negotiations led by Australia's Minister for Climate Change and Energy, Chris Bowen. A World Leaders' Summit is planned for November 11-12.

item.title: Uzbekistan May Restrict Methane Gas Station Operations Due to Cold Weather
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Energy announced potential restrictions on methane gas stations due to anticipated cold weather. Priority will be given to residential areas, schools, and hospitals. Seasonal consumers, including gas stations, may face temporary limitations based on approved schedules. Consumers will be notified in advance.

item.title: Uzbekistan Railways Marks 32nd Anniversary, Reports 9-Month Reform Results
item.description: Uzbekistan Railways celebrated its 32nd anniversary, highlighting achievements from the first nine months of the year. Reforms initiated by a presidential decree in October 2023 are enhancing the transport-logistics infrastructure. The company reports increased quality in passenger and cargo transport, construction, and industrial production, with digitalization reaching 75%.

item.title: Astana Pensioner's Eviction Halted for Heating Season Amidst Son's Debt Dispute
item.description: A pensioner in Astana will remain in her home during the heating season. Her apartment was sold to cover her son's debt of approximately 10 million tenge. The family sought help from Parliament members to halt the eviction, gaining time to pursue legal action regarding the disputed sale.

item.title: First-Year Journalism Student Dies in Almaty University Campus Dormitory
item.description: A first-year journalism student from Shymkent died in the dormitory of Almaty's Kazakh National University on November 6. Police and university officials are investigating the circumstances of her death. A criminal case has been initiated.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov Meets Residents of Tokmok and Chuy Region
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov met with residents of Tokmok city and the Chuy and Kemin districts during his working visit to the Chuy region. Citizens raised issues concerning rehabilitation centers, educational institutions, and agricultural loans. They also highlighted the need for improved roads and clean water supply.

item.title: Uzbek President Proposes Regional UN Counter-Terrorism Office in Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev proposed establishing a Regional UN Counter-Terrorism Office in Uzbekistan to help Central Asian nations combat terrorism using AI. The proposal was made at a security meeting in Astana, attended by leaders from Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Jordan, focusing on AI's role in security.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Tajikistan Presidents Inaugurate New Tajik Embassy in Astana
item.description: Presidents Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Emomali Rahmon attended the grand opening of the new Tajik Embassy in Astana. They cut the ceremonial ribbon, and the Presidential Orchestra performed the national anthems of both countries. The leaders also viewed a presentation about the embassy and planted saplings on the grounds.

item.title: Russian Billionaire Alexander Mashrabov Granted Kazakhstan Citizenship
item.description: Alexander Mashrabov, co-founder of AI startup Higgsfield, has received Kazakhstan citizenship. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev signed the decree on October 30. Mashrabov, who resided in the US, renounced his Russian citizenship as Kazakhstan law prohibits dual nationality. Higgsfield was valued at $5.4 billion.

item.title: Kazakhstan Supports Tajikistan's Election to UN Security Council
item.description: Kazakhstan officially supports Tajikistan's bid for election to the United Nations Security Council. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev expressed this support, highlighting the strong bilateral relations and shared interests between the two nations. This backing underscores Kazakhstan's commitment to regional stability and multilateralism.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Tajikistan Presidents Meet in Astana, Strengthen Ties
item.description: Kazakhstan President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev officially welcomed Tajikistan President Emomali Rahmon in Astana. The leaders discussed increased trade, with bilateral turnover exceeding $1 billion annually, making Kazakhstan a top trade partner for Tajikistan. They also noted expanding cultural and humanitarian ties and attended the opening of Tajikistan's new embassy.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Support Tajikistan's UN Security Council Candidacy
item.description: Kazakhstan will support Tajikistan's bid for a non-permanent seat on the UN Security Council for 2028-2029, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev announced after talks with Emomali Rahmon in Astana. The leaders also discussed security in Central Asia and agreed to jointly promote shared interests on international platforms.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Court Denies Home Arrest for Activist Facing Trial
item.description: A court in Bishkek has again denied home arrest for activist Tilekmat Kudaibergen uulu, who was brought from Dubai. Human rights defender Rita Karasarova stated that according to Kyrgyz law, individuals should be released if a verdict is not reached within a year of their case being sent to court. The judge cited the severity of the charges as a reason for not changing the pre-trial detention.

item.title: UN: Over 700 Health Facilities Closed in Afghanistan Due to Aid Cuts
item.description: The UN reports that more than 700 health facilities in Afghanistan have closed between 2025 and 2026 due to reduced international aid. Humanitarian funding has dropped significantly, limiting access to essential services. The UN criticized restrictions on female staff, which impact operations, and called for continued humanitarian assistance amid the worsening crisis.

item.title: Abay Region Akimat Illegally Obligated Market Owners to Cede Land for Free
item.description: The prosecutor's office in the Abay region has identified an illegal intervention by the Makanchy district akimat, which unlawfully required market owners to provide land for free. This violated entrepreneurs' rights. The illegal decree has been revoked, and the responsible official faces administrative penalties.

item.title: Russian Billionaire Alexander Mashrabov Granted Kazakhstani Citizenship
item.description: Russian billionaire Alexander Mashrabov, co-founder of AI startup Higgsfield, has obtained Kazakhstani citizenship. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev signed the decree on October 30. Mashrabov, who resided in the US, renounced his Russian citizenship as Kazakhstan law prohibits dual nationality. Higgsfield, valued at $5.4 billion, was founded in 2023.

item.title: Uzbekistan Factory Exceeds Environmental Emission Standards, Fined
item.description: A factory in Bekabad, Uzbekistan, has been found to exceed environmental emission norms, resulting in a compensation payment of 1.63 billion soms. Inspections revealed significant overages in dust, sulfur dioxide, and carbon monoxide emissions. The National Committee for Ecology and Climate Change mandated equipment upgrades and improved monitoring.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov Reviews Industrial Projects in Chu Region
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov visited the Chu region, reviewing plans for a new industrial zone spanning 202 hectares with an expected investment of 31.64 billion soms. He also inspected a cement plant under construction in the Kemin district, set to create 700 jobs. The president addressed land allocation issues in several districts.

item.title: Kazakhstan Supports Tajikistan's Candidacy for UN Security Council Non-Permanent Seat
item.description: Kazakhstan will support Tajikistan's bid for a non-permanent seat on the UN Security Council for 2028-2029. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev highlighted cultural and educational cooperation, noting Kazakhstan offers 100 educational grants annually to Tajik students and will continue training Tajik military personnel. Both nations share common interests on regional and global agendas.

item.title: Butun Kyrgyzstan Party to Support Ishak Masaliev's Presidential Candidacy
item.description: The political party 'Butun Kyrgyzstan' has announced its full support for Ishak Masaliev's candidacy in the upcoming presidential elections. Party leader Adakhan Madumarov confirmed the decision. Masaliev is the fifth candidate to officially register with the Central Election Commission, with the nomination period closing on November 13. The elections are scheduled for January 27, 2027.

item.title: Muslim World League Denounces Houthi Attacks on Saudi Holy Cities
item.description: The Muslim World League has condemned Houthi attacks targeting Mecca and Medina, stating they violate the sanctity of the holy cities. Secretary-general Al-Issa called the strikes a betrayal of religion and Muslims. The league expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia and supported its efforts to protect civilians and holy sites.

item.title: Trump Confirms US Military Strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island
item.description: US President Donald Trump confirmed American military strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island. This follows reports from Iranian media stating two missiles hit the Suza area. The confirmation comes amid ongoing indirect negotiations between the US and Iran, reportedly aimed at a new ceasefire and resuming nuclear talks.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Tajikistan Transit Cargo Volume Reaches 7 Million Tons
item.description: Transit cargo volume between Kazakhstan and Tajikistan via road and rail reached approximately 7 million tons last year, marking an 8% and 15% increase respectively. Both presidents emphasized the importance of revitalizing transport partnerships and agreed to digitalize transport systems for seamless cargo delivery.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Tajikistan Adopt Trade Roadmap Towards 2030
item.description: Kazakhstan and Tajikistan have adopted a roadmap to increase bilateral trade turnover to $2 billion by 2030. Presidents Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Emomali Rahmon agreed to expand cooperation in agriculture, energy, oil and gas, and manufacturing. Kazakhstan is now among Tajikistan's top three foreign trade partners.

item.title: Truck Falls Off Mountain Pass on Too-Ashu
item.description: A video circulating on social media shows a damaged truck at the foot of a mountain slope on the Too-Ashu pass, with its cargo scattered. The circumstances of the incident and whether there were any casualties are currently unknown and being clarified.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Tajikistan Presidents Hold Press Briefing, Emphasize Cooperation
item.description: The Presidents of Kazakhstan and Tajikistan held a joint press briefing, highlighting positive dynamics in bilateral cooperation. President Tokayev noted the significant progress made by both nations since gaining independence and emphasized the absence of unresolved issues, focusing instead on mutual progress.

item.title: Over 10 Million Liters of Substandard Gasoline Detected at Uzbek Gas Stations
item.description: During inspections in the first ten months of 2016, over 10 million liters of substandard Ai-92 gasoline were identified at gas stations across Uzbekistan. Approximately 3,000 stations were checked, with 330 found to be selling fuel that did not meet quality standards, primarily in Andijan and Fergana regions.

item.title: UN Official: ISIS-K Has Acquired Advanced Tactical Equipment, Including Drones
item.description: A UN counter-terrorism official stated that the ISIS-K branch has obtained advanced tactical equipment, including drones, and its members have completed training for their use. The official also noted that terrorist groups exploit online platforms for recruitment, making Central Asian countries vulnerable. ISIS-K reportedly uses Telegram and TikTok for communication and funding.
